# Review all tests — test-suite value audit with reproducible skill

## Summary

Review the entire (~476-file) test suite to evaluate whether each test actually tests something useful, classify every file against the documented low-value anti-pattern categories, produce a recommended removal/clean-up list, convert each recommendation into a child work item, and author a repo-local skill that makes the review process reproducible.

## Problem statement

The test suite has grown to ~476 `*.test.ts` files (~139k lines) — 364 unit, 112 browser, 12 E2E (incl. 6 tutorial-E2E parts), 4 smoke, plus balance/electron/scripts/replay groups — since the last full-suite cleanup (CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR removed 32 low-value files from a 344-file suite). Low-value tests (placeholder assertions, source-code-grep tests, self-referential simulations, duplicates of core coverage, type-level-only checks, zero-assertion browser tests) accumulate silently, adding maintenance cost and runtime without detecting real regressions. This item performs a fresh, reproducible audit of the whole suite and converts findings into actionable tracked work.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainers** — want a defensible, recorded basis for pruning the suite and assurance that kept tests add value.
- **AI agents / future reviewers** — need a codified, repeatable procedure so a re-audit (after more growth) is a skill invocation, not a from-scratch investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Entire-suite review completed.** Every `*.test.ts` file (all ~476, across unit/browser/E2E/smoke/balance/electron/scripts/replay) is reviewed and classified as `keep` / `remove` / `clean-up` against the anti-pattern categories reused from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR: source-code-grep assertions, placeholder/tautological tests (`expect(true).toBe(true)`), self-referential simulations (zero production-code imports), duplicates of core coverage, type-level/structural-only tests, and zero-assertion browser tests. *Verification:* a complete classification table (file → category/decision) is present in the report, and the reviewed file count reconciles with the inventory snapshot recorded at implementation start.
- **Removal & clean-up list delivered.** A categorised list of proposed removals/clean-ups is produced as `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` and summarised in the work-item description, each entry listing file path, line count, category, and rationale. *Verification:* the report exists, is committed, and its per-category counts reconcile with the classification table.
- **Recommendations tracked as child work items.** Each removal/clean-up recommendation is created as a child work item under CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y, each with a clear goal + measurable ACs, e.g.:
  ```bash
  wl create --parent CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --issue-type task --priority low --stage idea \
    --title "Test review: remove <group>" --description "…" --json
  ```
  **No test file is deleted or modified by this item itself** — the children carry out the changes. *Verification:* `wl show CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y --children --json` lists the recommendation items and the repo diff for this item contains no test deletions/edits (only report, skill, docs).
- **Reproducible skill authored.** A repo-local skill `/skill:test-review` is created at `.pi/skills/test-review/SKILL.md` (project skill conventions: front-matter `name` + `description`, markdown body, optional `scripts/`) codifying the methodology — anti-pattern categories, the exact discovery commands (grep/find patterns), classification steps, report format, and the child-work-item creation convention. *Verification:* the skill's documented procedure is exercised end-to-end during implementation to reproduce (a subset of) the audit on a clean checkout, and the skill is registered in docs.
- **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes — the review process, report, and the new `test-review` skill referenced in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and/or `AGENTS.md`. *Verification:* docs committed in the same change; no stale references to reviewed/removed files remain.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** (Release quality gate; `npm test -- --project unit` minimum before push — see AGENTS.md.) *Verification:* `npm test -- --project unit` is green at completion.

## Constraints

- Investigation scope is the **entire** suite (producer-confirmed); no area of the repo is exempt.
- This item is analysis + recommendation + skill authoring only — it must not itself remove or modify tests (producer-confirmed deliverable shape: create work items for recommendations).
- Reuse the anti-pattern categories and reporting style of CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR for continuity (producer-confirmed); this is a fresh pass over the grown suite, not a duplicate.
- Tests guarding historical regressions, documented precedents (e.g. the 2026-07-31 cleanup's reference list), and tests with explicit work-item linkage should be treated as `keep` unless evidence shows they no longer assert anything.
- UK English in all written output; work-item descriptions/comments in Markdown; ignore-rule compliance when scanning the repo.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Subjective classification risk (scope: whole review).** "Useful" is a judgement call. *Mitigation:* every classification carries an evidence line (file, lines, category, observed pattern); when evidence is ambiguous the file defaults to `keep` and is noted as `uncertain` rather than proposed for removal. Median, conservative posture — prefer a false negative to a false removal.
- **Risk of deleting a regression guard.** *Mitigation:* flagged removals are recommendations only and are executed by child work items through the normal implement → audit gate; a reviewer sees the full list before any deletion lands.
- **Browser/E2E static-review limits.** The 112 browser + 12 E2E files cannot be valued purely by static inspection. *Assumption:* classification there uses structure/assertion inspection and run-cost evidence; anything uncertain is `keep` with a `needs-manual-verification` note.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The review will surface adjacent opportunities (test-helper deduplication, fixture consolidation, runtime tuning). *Mitigation:* record these as separate linked work items (`discovered-from:CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y`), never as additional scope inside this item.
- **Inventory drift.** The suite grew from 344 → 476 files between cleanups and will keep growing. *Assumption:* the reviewed snapshot is the commit at implementation start, and the report records that commit hash; the new skill is the mechanism for refreshing the audit later.
- **Skill-staleness risk.** A written procedure can drift from the suite it describes. *Mitigation:* the skill documents the discovery commands and the report format, and the report records inventory counts, so a re-run diffs cleanly.
- **Overlap risk with CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR.** *Mitigation:* the report treats the 2026-07-31 removals as already-handled and re-audits only what exists today; near-misses are compared against that item's taxonomy for consistency.

## Existing state

- 476 `*.test.ts` files (~139k lines) under `tests/` across unit/browser/E2E/smoke/balance/electron/scripts/replay groups (counts verified at intake, 2026-09-15).
- Prior full-suite cleanup: CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR (completed, 2026-07-31) removed 32 files (~3,806 lines) and stripped dead assertions from 8 kept files; its category list is the reference taxonomy for this audit.
- Preliminary find at intake: `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts` (721 lines) contains 30 `expect(true).toBe(true)` placeholder branches behind a "function landed yet?" `require()` probe; the guarded functions (`resolveStaffApplicant`, `hireStaffApplicant`, `declineStaffApplicant`, `letGoStaffMember`) now exist in `MainStreetEngine.ts` (lines 3103–3203), so the guards are dead code and the `require` probe may be vacuous under Vitest ESM (`"type": "module"`). Prime removal/clean-up candidate to verify first.
- Repo-local skills precedent: `.pi/skills/release-windows/`, `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/` (front-matter + markdown body + optional `scripts/`); documented in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Desired change

- A committed, versioned audit report (`docs/dev/test-suite-review.md`) that a future agent can re-run and diff against.
- A `test-review` skill that automates/codifies the re-audit so the entire process is reproducible on demand.
- Child work items (one per recommendation or recommendation group) that carry out the removals/clean-ups through the normal implement workflow.

## Commands (copy-paste ready)

```bash
# Inventory snapshot (record the commit + counts in the report)
git rev-parse HEAD
find tests -name '*.test.ts' -type f | wc -l

# Discovery probes used for classification
grep -rc 'expect(true)\.toBe(true)' tests --include='*.test.ts' | grep -v ':0'
grep -rl 'readFileSync' tests --include='*.test.ts'

# Quality gate before push
npm test -- --project unit && npm run build
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` — the audit report (classification table + removal/clean-up list) — **new**
- `.pi/skills/test-review/SKILL.md` — the reproducible audit skill — **new** (optional `scripts/` helpers alongside)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` — reference the report and skill — **edited**
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts` — first confirmed candidate (clean-up/removal) — **touched by a child work item, not this item**
- `tests/**/*.test.ts` — the ~476 files reviewed (read-only here) — **reviewed**

## Related work

- **CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR** — Test suite cleanup: remove 32 low-value test files and strip dead assertions (completed; the taxonomy + precedent this audit extends).
- **CG-0MS9EJ3JT008ME4I** — Review testing patterns, CI/CD, and project infrastructure (completed).
- **CG-0MSZ4TN5Z001JADX** — Speed up browser tests and create test profiles (completed).
- **CG-0MSJ7ZXDB002CX97** — AGENTS.md: document when and how to run per-game, full-suite, and browser tests (completed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Does 'all tests' mean the *entire* suite (including the 112 browser tests and 12 E2E/tutorial files), or should the review be limited to the fast unit project?" — Answer (producer): "entire suite". Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q2: "Should this item deliver only a review artefact (removal list) with deletion deferred to a follow-up work item, or also execute removals here?" — Answer (producer): "create work items for recommendations". Interpretation: this item produces the report AND creates child work items carrying the removals; it does not itself delete/modify tests. Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q3: "Reuse the anti-pattern categories from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR? Confirm this is a fresh pass over the grown suite rather than a duplicate, and list any must-keep files/areas?" — Answer (producer): "confirmed". Interpretation: reuse the taxonomy; fresh pass over the ~476-file suite; no exempt areas. Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
- Q4 (new AC, added by producer): "Add a new AC which is to create a skill to make this process reproducible." — Answer (producer): directive to include AC4 (reproducible `test-review` skill). Source: interactive reply (2026-09-15).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQHAR5AF002XPYI** – Tests for reusable undo/redo button mechanism (completed)
- **CG-0MTH7COKM0004FCJ** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)
- **CG-0MQSF0385003SXHV** – [test-failure] main-street-tutorial-e2e.browser.test.ts: resource exhaustion after repeated Phaser game create/destroy cycles (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, added, adding (+317 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, added, adding (+248 more)

# Intake Brief — Staff effects need adjusting for new coin values (CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC)

## Problem statement

The integer-economy migration (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) scaled coin **data** ×100, but several staff cards were left behind: the Accountant still discounts market refreshes by `1` instead of `100`, and three staff descriptions still state pre-migration values (`1`). The Financial Advisor's advertised "reduces this business upgrade cost" ability was never implemented at all — there is no `upgradeCostDiscount` field, CSV column, parser, or engine wiring.

## Users

- **Player** — reads a staff card's text and pays the printed price; needs the discount they see to be the discount the engine applies.
- **Game designer / balancer** — needs `card-data.csv` and the engine to agree on the ×100 integer scale so economy tuning is trustworthy.
- **Developer / QA** — needs a durable guard that catches staff cost-reduction text/data drift and verifies the new Financial Advisor mechanic.

### User stories

- As a player, when I employ the Accountant I pay 100 less per market refresh, not 1.
- As a player, when I employ the Financial Advisor at a business, upgrading **that** business costs 100 less wherever I buy the upgrade (market, hand, or drag-and-drop).
- As a designer, I can read every staff description in `card-data.csv` and see amounts on the same ×100 scale as the data columns.
- As a developer, a failing unit test tells me exactly which staff card's cost-reduction text no longer matches its data column.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Accountant refresh discount corrected to the ×100 scale.** `card-data.csv` carries `refreshCostDiscount = 100` for `staff-accountant`; with an employed Accountant, `refreshMarketCost(state)` equals `REFRESH_MARKET_COST - 100`. Existing expectations that hard-code `1` (`tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts`, `balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`) are updated and pass.
2. **Financial Advisor `upgradeCostDiscount` implemented end-to-end.** A new `upgradeCostDiscount` staff field and `card-data.csv` column carry `100` for `staff-financial`; the parser populates it onto `StaffCard`. When a business employs a staff member with this discount, upgrading **that** business costs 100 less through every path — market purchase (`purchaseUpgrade` / `canPurchaseUpgrade`), hand play (`playUpgradeFromHand`), and drag-and-drop (`buyAndPlaceUpgrade` / `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade`) — while a business employing no such staff pays the full listed cost. The effective cost is floored at 0.
3. **Staff description text is ×100-consistent.** The Accountant ("cost 1 less" → "cost 100 less"), IT Specialist ("by 1" → "by 100"), Event Planner ("+1 synergy coin per turn" → "+100 synergy coin per turn"), and Financial Advisor ("by 1" → "by 100") descriptions no longer contain pre-migration single-digit coin values. IT Specialist and Delivery Driver remain **description-only** (not implemented); this is recorded in the brief and as a follow-up note so the gap is explicit, not silent.
4. **Automated regression guard for staff cost text.** A `unit`-profile test parses every staff cost-reduction description and asserts its amount equals the matching data column (`refreshCostDiscount` / `upgradeCostDiscount`) under the ×100 rule, failing with a message that identifies the offending card id.
5. **Tests, build, and documentation are green.** All affected unit tests pass, `npm run build` succeeds, and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` at minimum).

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`.** Apply the documented `×100 + round` rule from CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6; do not hand-rebalance other values in this item.
- **Financial Advisor scope is per-business** (Q1 decision): the discount applies only to the business where the Financial Advisor is employed, using `getEmployedStaffForBusiness(state, slotIndex)` / `business.employedStaff`.
- **IT Specialist and Delivery Driver are out of implementation scope** (Q4 decision). Only their description text is touched; `Delivery Driver` already reads `by 50` (correct) and `IT Specialist` is corrected to `by 100`. The unimplemented-effect gap must be captured (follow-up work item or explicit note in the description).
- **CSV schema addition is coordinated.** Adding `upgradeCostDiscount` requires updating `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`CsvRow`, `CSV_COLUMNS`, `NUMERIC_COLUMNS`) and inserting the column in the `card-data.csv` header at the position expected by `parseCsv` (immediately after `peekOncePerTurn`, before `art_notes`); the column-count assertions in `balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts` are updated in the same commit.
- **Pricing parity preserved.** The drag-and-drop +50% premium must be computed consistently with the click path. Define and document the order: discount the base cost first, then apply the premium.
- **No new RNG consumption; determinism and headless/AI parity preserved.** The AI affordability/value model must see the discounted upgrade cost so AI play is not disadvantaged.
- **Minimal churn** — touch only the staff/economy paths in scope; do not redesign the market or upgrade systems.

### Out of scope

- Implementing IT Specialist's refresh discount or Delivery Driver's purchase discount (Q4).
- Implementing the other nominal applicant perks (Barista, Bookkeeper, Customer Service Rep, Security Guard, etc.) — their live effects come from the random specialization-skill system.
- Rebalancing any other coin/reputation value.
- Adding a `purchaseCostDiscount` column (no current consumer).

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` staff rows:
  - `staff-accountant`: `refreshCostDiscount=1`, `taxAuditRate=0.25`, description "…makes investment refreshes cost 1 less…".
  - `staff-it`: no data column; description "Reduces this business refresh cost by 1.".
  - `staff-event-planner`: no data column; description "+1 synergy coin per turn from Entertainment businesses." (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` already states `+100`).
  - `staff-financial`: no data column; description "Reduces this business upgrade cost by 1.".
  - `staff-delivery`: no data column; description "Reduces business card purchase cost by 50 for this business." (already ×100-consistent).
- `StaffCard` (`MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) exposes `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `taxAuditRate`, `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn` — but **no** `upgradeCostDiscount`.
- `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` parses the staff columns above; it does not read an upgrade discount.
- `MainStreetMarketRefill.refreshMarketCost` sums every staff card's `refreshCostDiscount` plus the Negotiator skill and clamps at 0.
- Upgrade cost is charged from the raw `card.cost` in `canPurchaseUpgrade`, `purchaseUpgrade`, `playUpgradeFromHand`, `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade`, and `buyAndPlaceUpgrade` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`); no per-business discount exists.
- Per-business employed staff are available via `getEmployedStaffForBusiness(state, slotIndex)` (`MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) and `business.employedStaff`.
- `tests/main-street/card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` guards event, per-turn and ongoing-cost text/data consistency, but **not** staff cost-reduction descriptions.
- The nominal-job text of the 12 specialization applicants (CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ) was never implemented as literal per-card mechanics; their live effects come from the random specialization-skill system (`MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` / `MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`). This item deliberately implements only the Financial Advisor for now.

## Desired change

- Correct the Accountant's `refreshCostDiscount` from `1` to `100` in `card-data.csv` and fix its description.
- Add an `upgradeCostDiscount` staff field, CSV column, parser support, and per-business engine wiring for the Financial Advisor (`100`), covering all upgrade acquisition paths and the drag premium.
- Correct the four stale staff descriptions to the ×100 scale (Accountant, IT Specialist, Event Planner, Financial Advisor); leave IT Specialist and Delivery Driver mechanics unimplemented and documented as such.
- Extend the card-text consistency guard to staff cost-reduction descriptions.
- Update affected tests and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (and any other affected doc).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Accountant `refreshCostDiscount` 1 → 100; corrected descriptions; new `upgradeCostDiscount` column with `staff-financial = 100`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — add `readonly upgradeCostDiscount?: number` to `StaffCard`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the `upgradeCostDiscount` staff column into templates.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — add a pure `computeUpgradeCostDiscount(...)` helper (mirrors `computeRefreshCostDiscount` aggregation/floor semantics).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — apply the per-business discount in `canPurchaseUpgrade`, `purchaseUpgrade`, `playUpgradeFromHand`, `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade`, `buyAndPlaceUpgrade`; document discount-then-premium ordering.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — reuse `getEmployedStaffForBusiness` for the per-business lookup.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — use the effective (discounted) upgrade cost for affordability/value scoring.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — relies on the corrected Accountant value (no logic change expected).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts`, `example-games/main-street/gym/GymCardIndex.ts`, `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — surface the new field where staff abilities are displayed.
- `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` — `CsvRow`, `CSV_COLUMNS`, `NUMERIC_COLUMNS` for the new column.
- `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts`, `balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `staff-effect-scoping.test.ts`, `card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — update expectations and extend the guard; add a new Financial Advisor upgrade-discount test.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (and other affected `docs/main-street/*`) — correct the staff ability/description columns.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6** — Move to integer numbers for coins and reputation (completed): defined the ×100 rule this item completes for staff.
- **CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0** — Validate and fix all Main Street card text for the integer economy (in_review/completed): created the card-text/data consistency guard and corrected non-staff text; explicitly did **not** cover staff cost-reduction descriptions.
- **CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ** — Add 12 staff card templates to CSV (completed): introduced the specialization-applicant rows whose nominal descriptions drove this gap.
- **CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK** — Staff specialization epic: the random-skill system that is the live effect mechanism for applicants.
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** — Group F staff abilities: introduced the Accountant `refreshCostDiscount` column and its `1` value.
- **CG-0MTQ7W0ZX0059R3J** — Tax Audit 45%/25% with Accountant: implemented the Accountant `taxAuditRate` (already correct at `0.25`).
- **CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN** — Town Gossip peek / Lookout `peekOncePerTurn` — example of an implemented per-card staff ability.
- **CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP** — Upgrade drag-and-drop buy-and-place (+50% premium): the path that must apply the discount.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MO4LWXCK007PDCC** – Accessibility toggles & settings UI (completed)
- **CG-0MODJ4N4T004YO9I** – Update tests and smoke coverage for Phaser v4 migration (completed)
- **CG-0MUIH30NQ0047W1I** – Reconcile event card text to integer data (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — matched: advisor, cards, coin, cost, effects (+10 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: cards, coin, cost, effects, may (+9 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: cards, coin, cost, effects, may (+8 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: target-dependent affordability gate.** `canPurchaseUpgrade(state, cardId)` has no target slot, but the discount depends on which business is upgraded. Mitigation: resolve the target (or the best eligible discount) before the coin check and keep `can*`/`do*` paths in parity; test the case where only the discount makes an upgrade affordable.
- **Risk: drag-premium ambiguity.** Whether the +50% premium is applied before or after the discount changes the price. Mitigation: define **discount the base cost, then apply the premium**, document it in code, and assert it in tests.
- **Risk: CSV schema desynchronisation.** Adding a column can break `parseCsv`'s ordered header check and the balance-cards column-count tests. Mitigation: update `CsvRow`/`CSV_COLUMNS`/`NUMERIC_COLUMNS`, the CSV header, and the tests in one commit.
- **Risk: AI ignores the discount.** Mitigation: update `MainStreetAiStrategy` affordability/value to use the effective cost.
- **Risk: scope creep — implementing the other nominal staff perks.** The 12 applicant descriptions largely do not map to implemented mechanics; implementing them all would balloon this item. Mitigation: implement only the Financial Advisor; record the IT Specialist / Delivery Driver gap as an explicit follow-up.
- **Risk: per-business scoping confusion.** The discount must not leak street-wide (as happened historically with income buffs). Mitigation: look it up strictly through `getEmployedStaffForBusiness`.
- **Assumption:** multiple staff with `upgradeCostDiscount` at the same business stack additively and clamp at 0, mirroring `refreshCostDiscount`.
- **Assumption:** the discount applies to the base upgrade cost; the market display keeps the listed price unless a target business is known.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (producer review, prior run): "Financial Advisor's upgrade cost discount is NOT currently implemented — should I add a new `upgradeCostDiscount` field and implement the effect (discount applies when upgrading the business where the Financial Advisor is employed), value 100?" — **Answer (operator, interactive): "(a) Yes — add `upgradeCostDiscount`, wire it into `purchaseUpgrade`/`playUpgradeFromHand`, value 100." Source: interactive reply in this session.**
- Q2 (producer review, prior run): "IT Specialist and Delivery Driver effects are described but not implemented — implement these too, or focus only on the Financial Advisor and the Accountant value fix?" — **Answer (operator, interactive): "(a) Yes — implement both alongside Financial Advisor" (later narrowed by Q4). Source: interactive reply.**
- Q3: "Description text — fix all staff CSV description texts to use ×100 values?" — **Answer (operator, interactive): "(a) Yes — update ALL staff description text to the correct ×100 values." Source: interactive reply.**
- Q4: "IT Specialist's 'this business refresh cost' has no per-business refresh to target (single-row global market) and Delivery Driver's 'purchase cost for this business' cannot target an occupied employing slot — how should these behave?" — **Answer (operator, interactive): "(c) Drop IT Specialist & Delivery Driver from implementation scope; fix their CSV descriptions only." Source: interactive reply.**
- Q (prior run, unanswered before this session): "Accountant `refreshCostDiscount`: should this be `100`?" — **Answer (research + Q3): Yes.** Research: the migration rule is `value × 100`; the pre-migration value was `1`, and refresh-market tests use `REFRESH_MARKET_COST - 1`. Source: `card-data.csv`, `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts`, `git show 192943c9^:example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`.
- Q (prior run, unanswered before this session): "Other unimplemented staff effects?" — **Answer (Q4): IT Specialist and Delivery Driver remain description-only; Event Planner's stale `+1` description is corrected to `+100`.** Research: no engine code references `staff-it`, `staff-delivery`, or `staff-event-planner`; their live effects come from random specialization skills. Source: repo grep across `example-games/main-street/**/*.ts`.

# Intake Brief — REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own projects. (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17)

## Problem Statement

The Tableau Card Engine is a single flat monorepo where every example game is co-located with the shared engine code. This couples game development to the full repository, makes it hard to version or reuse the engine independently, and prevents building lean distributions that bundle only a selected subset of games.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer (primary)** — Maintains shared engine modules and the Gym demo suite; wants a standalone core-engine repo that can evolve, be versioned, and be pulled into any distribution without dragging all games along.
  - *Story:* As an engine maintainer I can work on `src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ui`, `src/ai` and the Gym in one repo, so that engine changes do not require touching game repos.
- **Game developer** — Builds a single example game in isolation; wants to check out just that game plus the engine and run `npm run dev` / `npm test` / `npm run build` without cloning every other game.
  - *Story:* As a game developer I can clone `tce-golf` (or any game repo) which pulls the core engine as a submodule, so that I can iterate on that game with a fast, focused checkout (`tce-game = distribution with 1 game`).
- **Distribution builder / launcher maintainer** — Assembles and ships a playable bundle (web + desktop binary) that contains the core engine plus a chosen set of 1..n games.
  - *Story:* As a distribution builder I can configure which game submodules are checked out in the launcher repo and run `npm run build` / `npm run package` to produce a web build and an Electron binary that show only the included games in the Game Selector.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Card outlines and card positions move when a card is added to the hand

## Problem Statement

When a `HandView` is configured with a known capacity (`maxSlots`) and ghost
position outlines (`showPositionOutlines: true`), both the card row **and** the
outline row are laid out relative to the *current* card count. Adding a card
therefore re-centres the whole row: every existing card and every slot shifts
laterally, and it only stops moving once the hand reaches `maxSlots`. The user
observes "the left card becomes centred and the two to the right are pushed
right; then when another card is added they all move left one slot".

Slot positions should be derived from the hand's **capacity**, not its current
size, so an occupied slot stays put as cards are added and the row only
re-lays when a slot is added (capacity change).

## Users

- **Player (Main Street, Gym)** — builds a stable spatial memory of where each
  held card sits; cards appear in the next free slot instead of shuffling under
  the pointer. Also keeps the ghost capacity outline in the same place as the
  card that later fills it.
- **Developer** — relies on `HandView` for layout; no scene-level workaround or
  bespoke hand rendering should be required to get stable slots.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, when I buy a second business card into my (capacity
  3) hand, the first card stays exactly where it was and the new card appears to
  its right.
- As a Gym user, drawing a 6th card into the 7-slot hand does not move the
  first five cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With `maxSlots` set, the set of outline slot positions for a given capacity
   is **identical** for a hand of 0, 1, … `maxSlots` cards (measured: the
   `outlineRects[i].x` for every `i` is unchanged across `setCards` of each
   size).
2. Adding a card places it in the next empty slot to the right of the occupied
   run, and every already-placed card keeps its pre-add position (measured:
   for `addCard`, `sprite[i].x` before === after for all pre-existing `i`).
3. Occupied outline slots still sit at the exact card position and rotation
   (`rect.x/y/rotation === sprite.x/y/rotation`), and extra capacity slots still
   render below every card — the CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680 invariant is preserved.
4. Changing capacity (`setMaxSlots(n)`) re-lays the whole row and always yields
   exactly `n` slots; this is the only mutation that may move existing cards.
5. The empty-hand capacity row is unchanged from today's behaviour — `maxSlots`
   straight/arc slots centred on the hand centre — so an empty hand still shows
   the full capacity in the same place the cards will occupy.
6. Unit tests (`tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`) verify AC 1–5, including a
   regression test that asserts positions do **not** move across successive
   `addCard`/`setCards` calls up to capacity, and that `setMaxSlots` does
   re-layout.
7. Browser tests (`tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts`,
   `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts`) assert slot/card position
   stability across a draw/add, not just alignment at a single hand size.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Hand capacity outlines), `AGENTS.md` if the
   documented behaviour changes, and any relevant Gym/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the shared `HandView` (`src/ui/HandView.ts`), not as a
  scene-specific workaround, because both Main Street and the Gym use
  `maxSlots` + outlines.
- Preserve the existing empty-hand capacity row (centred on `centerX`): that
  row *is* the fixed slot template, so no visual change is expected for an
  empty hand.
- The fix must honour the existing layout options: `spacing`, `maxWidth`
  compression, `arcRadius`, `maxRotationDegrees`, `cardWidth`/`cardHeight`,
  `centerX`, and both `horizontal` and `vertical` `layoutDirection`.
- Cards fill the capacity slots left-to-right; the row is not re-anchored per
  card count.
- The layout must remain deterministic (same inputs → same positions).
- Vertical cascade already derives positions from `baseY + i * spacing`, so it
  is already card-count independent; the change must not regress it.
- Over-capacity hands (transiently `cards.length > maxSlots`) are best-effort:
  the first `maxSlots` slots stay fixed, outlines stay capped at `maxSlots`,
  and overflow cards continue to the right with the same step. Normal gameplay
  prevents this state.

## Existing State

- `src/ui/HandView.ts`:
  - `computeCardPositions()` (≈ line 1719) computes the card row with
    `layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })` → the row is
    centred on the **current** card count, so it moves as cards are added.
  - `_computeOutlineSlots()` (≈ line 1299) handles two branches: with no cards
    it lays out the full `maxSlots` row (the desired fixed template); with cards
    it ghosts `computeCardPositions()` and appends extras to the right of the
    last card, so the occupied slots inherit the moving card layout.
  - `_outlineCount()` returns `maxSlots` when defined, else `cards.length`.
  - `_updateOutlinePositions()` / `applyLayout()` reposition and rebuild
    outlines on every mutation.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — already provides the centred, optionally
  compressed row maths needed to build a capacity template; no change expected.
- Main Street wires `showPositionOutlines: true`, `maxSlots:
  state.maxHandSize`, `centerX: handCenterX`, and syncs capacity with
  `setMaxSlots()` (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, `MainStreetRendererLayout.ts`).
- Gym wires `showPositionOutlines: true`, `maxSlots: 7` in
  `GymHandPileScene.ts`.
- Existing tests assert alignment at a *single* hand size but never stability
  across adds: `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`,
  `tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts`.

## Desired Change

- Compute the slot template once from capacity: when `maxSlots` is defined,
  derive the `maxSlots` row positions (using the same `layoutCardPositions` /
  arc maths used today for the empty-hand outline row) and place the first
  `this.cards.length` cards into it.
- Reuse that same template in `_computeOutlineSlots()` so occupied slots ghost
  their card positions and extra slots continue the template to the right —
  producing one consistent capacity row for both cards and outlines at every
  hand size.
- Keep `showPositionOutlines` purely visual: capacity-driven layout is keyed on
  `maxSlots !== undefined`, so toggling outlines off does not move cards.
- Leave hands that do not declare `maxSlots` on the existing centred-on-count
  layout.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`: derive card/outline positions from the `maxSlots` capacity template instead of `cards.length`.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — Likely unchanged; reused to build the capacity row.
- `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` — Add stability/regression tests (AC 1–5).
- `tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts` — Assert slot/card stability across a draw.
- `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts` — Assert stability across an added card; re-check click/drag/transfer paths that assume the hand centre.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Update "Hand capacity outlines" to document capacity-driven (stable) slot semantics.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — Help text only if the documented behaviour wording changes.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` / `MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — Verify no scene-level assumption about per-count centring; likely no code change.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680** — "Show an outline of card positions in the hand"
  (completed): introduced `showPositionOutlines` / `maxSlots` and the layout
  code this bug corrects.
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** — "Main Street: merge business hand + held event into
  one horizontal 3-card hand" (completed): established the 3-card hand and
  `handCenterX` anchoring.
- **CG-0MQSFGE540037N6S** / **CG-0MQRXO41D009DH26** — "Write Tests for Staff
  Cards & Hand Capacity" / "Implement Staff Cards & Hand Capacity System"
  (completed): runtime capacity changes that exercise `setMaxSlots`.
- **CG-0MS937FT9006273E** — "Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight renders over
  cards to the right" (completed): the depth-ordering pattern the outline
  depths build on.
- Automated `find-related` report (below) surfaced: CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7,
  CG-0MQ54PYAJ001XCUG, CG-0MLTFFGBH1CEPC7J (low signal for this layout bug).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (design):** The fixed slot row is the *same* centred capacity
  row currently rendered for an empty hand. Consequently a 1-card hand places
  that card in the **leftmost** capacity slot (left of the hand centre) rather
  than at the centre. This is the direct reading of "the position of the cards
  should not move unless a new slot is added", and it keeps the empty-hand
  appearance unchanged.
- **Assumption (scope):** Capacity-driven layout keys off `maxSlots !==
  undefined`, independent of whether outlines are currently visible, so
  toggling outlines never moves cards.
- **Assumption (right):** Cards fill capacity slots left-to-right; the row is
  never right- or centre-anchored per card count.
- **Risk:** Main Street's `handCenterX` anchoring and the hand→street transfer
  animation (`hiddenTransferSourceCardIds`) may assume a centred row for hit
  testing or source coordinates. Mitigation: run the Main Street browser suite
  and the drag/click/transfer flows; adjust only if a real regression appears.
- **Risk:** `maxWidth` compression means the step depends on `maxSlots`, so a
  capacity change can shift positions more than one slot. Acceptable — capacity
  change is an explicitly allowed re-layout.
- **Risk:** Over-capacity transient states. Mitigation: define best-effort
  behaviour above and unit-test it.
- **Scope creep guard:** Games without `maxSlots`, and any non-outline hand
  behaviour, must remain on the existing centred-on-count layout. A broader
  "slots everywhere" redesign (e.g. right-to-left hands, per-slot assignment)
  is out of scope and should be raised as a new work item if desired.

## Clarifying Questions & Answers (Appendix)

The seed context plus repository inspection answered the material design
questions; no operator/producer questions were required before drafting. The
resolutions are **agent assumptions** derived from the requirement (not
producer statements); each is labelled for confirmation during review:

- Q: Which layout should a capacity hand use? — **Assumption (agent):** the
  fixed centred capacity row already rendered for an empty hand, with cards
  filling it left-to-right. Evidence: `_computeOutlineSlots()` empty-hand
  branch already produces this row; the bug report only objects to the
  movement, implying the empty-hand row is acceptable. The only alternative
  (anchor slot 0 at the hand centre) would make the empty-hand outlines jump
  when the first card is drawn, so it does not satisfy "positions should not
  move".
- Q: Does the fix apply to the shared `HandView` or Main Street only? —
  **Assumption (agent):** shared `HandView`, keyed on `maxSlots`. Evidence:
  both `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` and `GymHandPileScene.ts` enable
  `maxSlots` + outlines and exhibit the same defect.
- Q: Should toggling outlines on/off move cards? — **Assumption (agent):** no;
  layout is keyed on capacity (`maxSlots`), not on `showPositionOutlines`.
- Q: What happens when a slot is added? — **Assumption (agent):** the row
  re-lays out (existing `setMaxSlots()` behaviour), which is the one case where
  movement is expected.
- **Producer confirmation requested (non-blocking):** the consequence of this
  design is that a 1-card hand shows its card in the **leftmost** capacity slot
  (off-centre) rather than centred. This is the only user-visible outcome that
  changes for existing scenes; it is logically required by "positions should
  not move unless a new slot is added".

## Related work (automated report)

- **CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7** – Implement Multi-Use Card Economy in Main Street (completed)

## Goal

Fix the shared `HandView` so that, when `maxSlots` is set, card and outline positions derive from the hand's **capacity** rather than the current card count — adding a card never moves an existing card or slot.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Sibling test items add the failing unit and browser tests first.

Root cause: `computeCardPositions()` builds a row centred on `this.cards.length` (`layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })`), and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts it (plus appending extras). The empty-hand branch already lays out the desired fixed `maxSlots` row, so that row is the template to reuse. `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path all re-derive the row/rotation normalisation from the occupied positions and must move to the template as well. `setMaxSlots()` currently only rebuilds outlines and does not re-lay the cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1–AC5: implement the capacity-template behaviour — outline slot positions identical for a hand of 0…`maxSlots` cards; `addCard` fills the next slot right of the occupied run while pre-existing card positions are unchanged; occupied outlines still match card `x/y/rotation` with extras below every card; `setMaxSlots(n)` is the only mutation that re-lays the row and always yields exactly `n` slots; the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged (same centred straight/arc row the cards will occupy).
- Add a shared private helper in `src/ui/HandView.ts` that derives the `maxSlots` template with the existing `layoutCardPositions` maths (gap = `spacing - cardWidth`, `centerX`, `maxWidth` compression, `arcRadius` Y) and the template-span rotation normalisation; recompute from current options on each use (no stale cache).
- `computeCardPositions()` horizontal returns the first `cards.length` template positions; over-capacity cards continue with the template step to the right (best-effort, no re-centring).
- `getInsertionPosition(index)` returns the template position at `index` (first `maxSlots`; template step beyond), so Market→hand transfer animations land exactly on the resting card.
- `_computeOutlineSlots()` derives all `count` slots from the same template (occupied slots ghost the card's **actual** sprite rotation, extras keep `depth = index - 0.5 - count`), replacing the per-count ghosting/extension branch.
- Rotation and arc normalisation in `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path use the template span when `maxSlots` is set, so per-card rotation is also stable across adds.
- `setMaxSlots(maxSlots)` re-lays the cards (calls `applyLayout()`), not just the outlines.
- Capacity-driven layout is keyed on `maxSlots !== undefined`, independent of `showPositionOutlines`; toggling outlines never moves cards.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout; vertical cascade keeps `baseY + i * spacing` and is not regressed.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` is reused unchanged.

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`, `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, `sortCards()` animated path, `setMaxSlots()`.

- Capacity-driven `HandView` layout with stable card and outline slots and green sibling tests.

# CI Windows binary ships no games: package.yml builds core-only, launch smoke asserts ≥9

**Discovered during:** `/skill:ship release` of v0.1.18 (PR #802) — release aborted at the PR CI gate (exit code 4).

## User story

As the release operator I can promote `dev` to `main` without the `package-windows` CI job failing, so that the primary Steam artifact (the Windows binary) ships with the intended, non-empty game catalogue.

## Problem

The merged-core refactor (epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17) removed the example games from this repo — `example-games/` now contains only `gym`, and the games live in sibling repos (`../tce-<game>`). The launcher's default build preset is `core-only` (`configs/core-only.json`, `games: []`).

`.github/workflows/package.yml` runs `npm run package:win`, which runs `npm run build:electron` with **no `GAMES_CONFIG`**, so it uses the `core-only` default. The packaged Windows binary therefore contains only the Gym (1 catalogue entry).

The packaged-binary launch smoke test asserts the full catalogue:

```
tests/electron/launch-smoke.test.ts:107
expect(info.catalogueCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(9);
```

so `package.yml` fails deterministically.

## Evidence

- Failed run: `Package Windows Binary` run 36448631082 (job 109017322638) on tag `v0.1.18` (commit `420ff075`).
  `AssertionError: expected 1 to be greater than or equal to 9` at `tests/electron/launch-smoke.test.ts:107`.
- PR #802 (`release/dev-to-main-20260928160435` → `main`) is open; `build` passed, `package-windows` failed; `mergeStateStatus: UNSTABLE`.
- `dev` is **not** merged into `main` — the release did not land.
- The same core-only default affects `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (Pages), tracked by CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1.

## Root cause

`package.yml` packages the **core-only** preset. There is no step that composes the sibling game repos (`.gitmodules` does not exist; the distribution is sibling-only per `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`), so CI cannot build the full catalogue as written. The smoke test's hard-coded `>= 9` no longer matches the default preset.

## Decision required (production intent)

Should the Windows binary (the primary Steam artifact) ship:

- **(A) The full distribution** — then `package.yml` must compose the game repos (`npm run setup:distribution -- --dir ..`, the eight `tce-*` remotes exist and are public) and build with `GAMES_CONFIG=full`; the smoke assertion should be derived from the selected preset.
- **(B) A core-only launcher** — then the smoke assertion must match the configured preset (≥1 for `core-only`), and the "primary Steam artifact" intent must be reconciled (games would arrive later via the runtime plugin loader, CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5).
- **(C) Something else / defer** — record the decision and adjust the workflow + test accordingly.

Until this is decided the CI job cannot be made green and the release is blocked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The intended game catalogue for the Windows binary is decided and recorded on this work item (A, B, or C above).
- **AC2:** `.github/workflows/package.yml` produces a binary whose Game Selector catalogue matches that decision on a clean CI checkout (all bundled presets resolved or siblings composed as required; no silent fallback).
- **AC3:** The packaged-binary launch smoke test (`tests/electron/launch-smoke.test.ts`) asserts the catalogue derived from the **selected preset**, not a hard-coded `>= 9`, so it cannot silently drift again.
- **AC4:** `RELEASE.md` (and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` if affected) describes the packaging preset and any distribution-composition step consistently, in the same commit (per the project doc-update policy).
- **AC5:** The `package-windows` job passes on a clean CI run of the fixing commit, and the full test suite is green at that commit (release gate).

## Related work

- Parent epic: CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 (merged-core refactor)
- CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1 — Pages deploy should use `GAMES_CONFIG=full` (same default-preset gap, different workflow)
- CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5 — Electron runtime game plugin loader (deferred mechanism for shipping games with the binary)
- Release PR: https://github.com/TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine/pull/802

# Intake Brief — Update AGENTS.md for the split multi-repo structure and cross-repo change guidance (CG-0MUMAIIT40002MRP)

## Problem Statement

`AGENTS.md` advertises the split multi-repo topology but still points at game
sources under `example-games/<game>/…` that no longer exist in the core
checkout (only `example-games/gym/` remains), and it gives no guidance on
whether an agent working in the core repo may touch sibling game repos. Agents
therefore either follow stale paths or treat sibling games as out-of-bounds —
blocking the core↔game co-evolution the split was meant to enable.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer / agent working in the core repo (primary)** — needs
  `AGENTS.md` to describe the real topology (merged core + `tce-*` sibling
  repos; each game repo composes the core as a `./core` submodule) and to
  explicitly permit appropriate changes in sibling game repos.
  - *Story:* As an agent working in the core repo, I can make an engine API
    change and update the affected sibling game repo(s), run their tests and
    push them, so core and games do not silently drift.
- **Game developer working in a `tce-<game>` repo** — needs to know the shared
  conventions still apply and how the core is composed; the cross-repo guidance
  makes explicit what the core may change in their repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `AGENTS.md` accurately describes the split topology: the core repo (engine +
   Gym + launcher shell + distribution) with game repos as **sibling
   `tce-<game>` checkouts**, each composing the core as a `./core` git
   submodule; the core carries no games at HEAD except the Gym. Wording matches
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` and `README.md`.
2. Cross-repo working guidance is added to the **existing** *Project-specific
   guidance* and *Worklog Rules* sections (option B — no new top-level
   section): an agent working in the core repo may and should make appropriate
   changes in sibling game repos, including editing, running tests, building,
   committing, and pushing to the game repo's `dev` branch (**never `main`**),
   and using that repo's Worklog store when one exists (otherwise recording the
   cross-repo change on the core work item).
3. All stale in-body game paths are corrected to the sibling layout — e.g.
   `example-games/main-street/…` → `../tce-main-street/src/…`,
   `example-games/golf/…` → `../tce-golf/src/…`, plus the `blackjack` and
   `coloretto` references; remaining `example-games/` references are Gym-only.
4. The mandated context-budget artifacts stay consistent: the threshold file is
   refreshed in the same commit (pre-push gate + guard test).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Documentation-only change (issue type `chore`); no code behaviour change.
- `AGENTS.md` is loaded every session and is **size-gated**: keep additions
  concise, and refresh `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` in the same
  commit (exact-match convention; the guard test fails on drift).
- Follow the doc-update policy; write in UK English.
- Guidance must not weaken safety/gates: pushes still target `dev` only, and
  the build → test → commit order and `wl`-only work-item mutations still hold.
- No new top-level `AGENTS.md` section (operator chose option B).

## Existing State

- `AGENTS.md` already has an opening paragraph, a *Directory Structure* section
  and an *Example Games* component bullet describing the split (core +
  `tce-<game>` siblings, `./core` submodule).
- Six stale non-gym game-path references remain (lines 251, 281, 284, 340,
  346, 469).
- There is no statement that an agent working in core may modify sibling game
  repos (edit/test/push/worklog).
- No sibling game repo currently ships an active Worklog database;
  `../tce-main-street/.worklog/` holds only a leftover `worktrees/` directory
  — so the “if a worklog exists” clause is forward-looking.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` (merged-core / Option A) and `README.md`
  describe the sibling topology and are the reference for the corrected wording.

## Desired Change

- Tighten the structure prose / *Example Games* bullet to unambiguously state
  the sibling topology and the submodule direction (game → core at `./core`;
  the core never submodules games).
- Add concise cross-repo-change guidance in *Project-specific guidance* and in
  *Worklog Rules / TCE Project Conventions*.
- Correct the six stale game paths to `../tce-<game>/src/…`.
- Refresh `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS.md` — structure description, cross-repo guidance, stale-path fixes.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — regenerated threshold (mandatory

- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — reference only; align wording only if

- `README.md` — consistency check; fix only if the `AGENTS.md` change exposes a contradiction.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — consistency check; fix only if the `AGENTS.md` change exposes a contradiction.
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — context-budget refresh/check script backing the pre-push gate (AC4).
- `tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts` — guard test for the committed thresholds (runs in the unit profile) (AC4).
- `.githooks/pre-push` — pre-push gate enforcing the context-budget thresholds (AC4).
- `package.json` — `context:check` / `context:refresh` npm script entries for the gate (AC4).

## Related Work

- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own projects. (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17)` — open, `plan_complete` — parent epic; this item contributes to its docs AC.
  - `Documentation for multi-repo workflow (CG-0MTRO7BFQ003IN2X)` — completed (F6) — the original multi-repo doc update, including `AGENTS.md`.
  - `Merge the core into Tableau-Card-Engine (Option A): games compose it as ./core, distribution composes siblings (CG-0MUJ0IAJM009X0Q2)` — completed — established the merged-core topology this brief documents.
  - `Write the Option A decision record and update the multi-repo architecture docs (CG-0MUJ0IJ6300398VR)` — completed.

  `.pi/`/`skill/`/agent-infrastructure — not sibling product repos.

## Problem

The ship skill's post-release close step (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js`) refuses to close a release candidate whose `wl close --force` would sweep **any** descendant that is not itself a candidate in the same release:

```js
const candidateIds = new Set(toClose.map((item) => item.id));   // = items currently at stage=in_review
const collateral = descendants.filter((id) => !candidateIds.has(id));
if (collateral.length > 0) refuse(...);
```

Because `getCandidateItems()` only returns items at `stage=in_review`, a descendant that is already `stage=done` (shipped in a previous release) or `deleted` is **never** a candidate — so it is always counted as collateral and the parent is refused. Net effect: any parent with a child that shipped in an earlier release can never be auto-closed by the ship step and gets stuck at `status=completed, stage=in_review` indefinitely.

The guard was introduced by SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H AC9/AC10 to avoid sweeping *out-of-scope* (non-terminal) work; terminal descendants (done/deleted) are harmless to sweep and should not trigger a refusal.

## Evidence (v0.1.19 release, 2026-10-02)

3 of the 5 refused items were refused **only** because their descendants are already terminal:

| Parent | Blocking descendants | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| Staff effects need adjusting for new coin values (CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC) | 3 `deleted` children | all work terminal |
| Quality Improvement - Refactoring (CG-0MUEUWE8400951Z9) | 2 `done` children (closed 2026-09-29) | all work terminal |
| Review all tests (CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y) | 1 `done` child (CG-0MU9POD4X003ZCOU, closed 2026-09-28 / v0.1.18) | all work terminal |

The other 2 refused items (CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ, CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17) are legitimate: they have open/blocked children and were moved to `in_review` prematurely.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The refusal predicate ignores descendants that are already terminal (`status=deleted`, or `stage=done` / `status=completed`), so a parent whose remaining descendants are all closed can be closed by the release step.
2. A parent with any non-terminal descendant (open/in-progress/blocked/in_review-not-yet-closed-in-this-release) is still refused, with the non-terminal descendants reported.
3. Unit tests cover: parent + already-done child → closed; parent + deleted child → closed; parent + open child → refused.
4. The v0.1.19 stragglers (CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC, CG-0MUEUWE8400951Z9, CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y) can be closed once the fix lands (or are closed manually as a one-off).

## Notes

- This is a **global agent skill** (`~/.pi/agent/skills/ship`), not repo code — file here as the originating project record; the fix belongs in the skill repository.
- Related: SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H (scope guard), SA-0MUAL2NQV0008HY5 (force-close rationale).
